From Puckline Press

Puckline Press article

Frozen Frenzy, explained: the night all 32 NHL teams play

Tuesday's 16-game Frozen Frenzy was the fourth in a row. Here's what the event is, where it came from, how rare it is, and how last night went.

By Puckline Prince · Oct 14, 2026 · Article page

Read the article

Every NHL team played on Tuesday night. That's the Frozen Frenzy: one evening, 16 games, all 32 clubs, and a new puck drop almost every 15 minutes from 6 p.m. Eastern until the last game started at 11. ESPN says this was the fourth year in a row it has put the event on.

The Frozen Frenzy is a scheduling showcase built with ESPN. The league gives the night a full slate, then spreads the start times out so the games overlap as little as possible. ESPN carries a tripleheader on its main channel (6 p.m., 8:30 p.m. and 11 p.m. Eastern), and the other 13 games stream on its services.

The centrepiece is a whip-around studio show that jumps from rink to rink for goals, big hits and late finishes, the hockey version of the NFL's RedZone. In the first edition, John Buccigross and Kevin Weekes hosted it, and the show ran about six and a half hours across ESPN+ and ESPN2.

This year's tripleheader was Devils at Red Wings at 6, Avalanche at Stars at 8:30 and Bruins at Sharks at 11. The other games started every 15 minutes from 6:15 to 9 p.m., then at 9:45 (Flames at Ducks) and 10:30 (Oilers at Kings), so all 16 games had their own start time.

A night with all 32 teams in action is newer than you might think. The first 16-game day in NHL history was Saturday, April 8, 2023, the last Saturday of the 2022-23 regular season. That day started at 12:30 p.m. Eastern and was not branded as anything.

The first Frozen Frenzy came six months later, on Tuesday, Oct. 24, 2023. NHL.com called it the second 16-game day in league history. ESPN's tripleheader that night was Maple Leafs at Capitals, Bruins at Blackhawks (Connor Bedard's rookie season) and Flyers at the Golden Knights, the defending Stanley Cup champions.

Since then it has become a fixture of October:

  • Oct. 24, 2023: the first Frozen Frenzy
  • Oct. 22, 2024: opened with Capitals at Flyers, closed with Kings at Golden Knights
  • Oct. 28, 2025: opened with Penguins at Flyers, closed with Kings at Sharks
  • Oct. 13, 2026: opened with Devils at Red Wings, closed with Bruins at Sharks

All four have been on a Tuesday.

Nights like this are rare. Before the 2024 edition, NHL.com counted only three earlier days with all 32 teams playing: April 8, 2023, the first Frozen Frenzy, and Jan. 13, 2024. It also said the 2024 Frenzy would be the only day that season with every team in action.

So the Frenzy is the one guaranteed 16-game night on the calendar, and in some seasons it has been the only one.

The 2026 edition delivered 112 goals in 16 games, an average of seven a game. Road teams won nine of the 16. Three games went past regulation: the Devils won in overtime in Detroit, 5-4, and the Canadiens (over Buffalo, 4-3) and Kraken (in Philadelphia, 3-2) both won in shootouts.

All the final scores:

  • Devils 5, Red Wings 4 (OT)
  • Panthers 7, Blue Jackets 3
  • Canadiens 4, Sabres 3 (SO)
  • Hurricanes 4, Capitals 2
  • Kraken 3, Flyers 2 (SO)
  • Rangers 4, Lightning 1
  • Blues 7, Senators 2
  • Islanders 3, Canucks 2
  • Blackhawks 5, Penguins 3
  • Jets 5, Wild 2
  • Avalanche 3, Stars 2
  • Golden Knights 5, Predators 2
  • Mammoth 5, Maple Leafs 4
  • Flames 4, Ducks 2
  • Oilers 4, Kings 1
  • Bruins 6, Sharks 3

The most lopsided results were Florida's 7-3 win in Columbus and St. Louis's 7-2 win in Ottawa. In the 8:30 headliner, Colorado beat Dallas 3-2 in regulation, and Boston closed the night with six goals in San Jose.

Full recaps of every game are on the Last night page.

Friday, November 6

Game recap

UTA4MTL5OTFinal: UTA 4, MTL 5 OT

Logan Cooley scored a hat trick and added an assist, Utah led three separate times, and the Mammoth still flew out of Montreal with one point. Cooley went 9, 10, 11 on the season, two of them on the power play, and Nick Schmaltz's power-play goal made it 4-3 early in the third. Every time, the Canadiens came back: Nick Suzuki (a goal, two assists), Arber Xhekaj, who scored his first and then dropped the gloves with Liam O'Brien four seconds later, Kirby Dach, and Adam Engstrom, whose first of the year tied it 4-4 with five minutes left. Cole Caufield needed 30 seconds of overtime for his 11th, set up by Lane Hutson and Suzuki. Jakub Dobes stopped only 16 of 20, Sebastian Cossa 30 of 35. Montreal is 10-3-3. Utah held the lead for most of the night and handed it back three times: that's not a lead, that's a timeshare.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

VGK2DET1Final: VGK 2, DET 1

Forty minutes of nothing, then a third period worth the price of admission, and Vegas took it 2-1 in Detroit. Anton Johansson finally broke the ice for the Red Wings two minutes into the third, and the lead lasted all of 2:18 before Braeden Bowman tied it. Then, with 1:42 left, Trevor Connelly buried his seventh from Jack Eichel and Rasmus Andersson, and the Little Caesars Arena crowd went home with cold pizza. Carter Hart was the reason it got that far, stopping 25 of 26, while Daniil Tarasov made 32 saves on 34 shots in a game the Wings had no business staying in. Vegas is 11-5-2. Detroit falls to 7-7-3, one goal on a night it needed two. Hockeytown has been rebuilding so long the blueprints are on microfiche.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

CHI1TBL4Final: CHI 1, TBL 4

Tampa Bay is now 8-0 at home, and Chicago never looked like the team to change that. Victor Hedman opened it on the power play four minutes in, Ilya Mikheyev scored late in the first, and early in the third Ryan McDonagh and Mikheyev again made it 4-0 inside three minutes. Zemgus Girgensons came back from his lower-body injury ahead of schedule and set up Mikheyev's second. Andrei Vasilevskiy stopped 25 of 26, and the one he missed was Roman Kantserov's with 50 seconds left, which is the closest thing to a highlight the Blackhawks had. Dillon Boucher and Jeffrey Viel fought early in the second. Arvid Soderblom made 31 saves on 35 shots. The Lightning are 10-3-2. Chicago is 4-12-1, and in a rebuild like this, spoiling the shutout counts as a win.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

STL4NJD5OTFinal: STL 4, NJD 5 OT

New Jersey led 4-1 after two periods and still needed Jesper Bratt in overtime. The Devils built it with a goal from Luke Hughes, two from Anthony Mantha and one from Jesper Boqvist, with Mantha's second coming 19 seconds after Boqvist's; Jack Hughes had two assists. Then St. Louis woke up. Mason McTavish scored midway through the third, Philip Broberg made it 4-3, and Dalibor Dvorsky tied it 18 seconds later with 5:06 to go. Bratt settled it 1:26 into overtime, from Dougie Hamilton. Connor Hellebuyck stopped 28 of 32, and Jordan Binnington made 31 saves on 36 shots. Jake Neighbours and Timo Meier fought early in the second. The Devils are 11-5-0. The Blues scored three goals in 3:08 to rescue a game they'd spent two periods losing, then got a loser point for it, which is the most St. Louis outcome possible.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

CAR5NYI3Final: CAR 5, NYI 3

Carolina scored twice in the first 3:20, the Islanders tied it twice, and the league's best team won it anyway, 5-3 at UBS Arena. Logan Stankoven scored 57 seconds in and Jesperi Kotkaniemi added another. Mitchell Chaffee (his first) and Brayden Schenn tied it early in the second; Andrei Svechnikov put Carolina back in front a minute later, and Victor Eklund tied it again before the second intermission. The winner came from the least likely name on the sheet: William Carrier, his first of the season with 5:08 left, from Svechnikov and Sebastian Aho. Jalen Chatfield added the empty-netter. Brandon Bussi stopped 24 of 27, Semyon Varlamov 34 of 38. The Hurricanes are 13-3-2. The Islanders, still without Mathew Barzal and Ryan Pulock, are 7-6-2, and they made their fans watch a fourth-liner decide it.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

PHI2NYR3Final: PHI 2, NYR 3

Philadelphia had a third-period lead at Madison Square Garden and gave it back in 89 seconds. Gabe Perreault scored first for the Rangers, then Simon Benoit (his first of the year) and Noel Acciari scored two minutes apart in the second to put the Flyers up 2-1. It held until 13:52 of the third, when Pavel Dorofeyev tied it on the power play, and Tye Kartye won it at 15:21, with Adam Fox assisting on both. Dylan Garand stopped 23 of 25 for New York, and Joseph Woll made 25 saves on 28 shots for Philadelphia. The Rangers are 9-7-1. The Flyers fall to 4-10-4. For an offense that scores less than anyone, two goals is a hot streak, and they still couldn't hold it through the third.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

BOS6PIT2Final: BOS 6, PIT 2

Justin Brazeau gave Pittsburgh a 1-0 lead nine minutes in, and Boston answered with six of the next seven goals. Pavel Zacha, Mark Kastelic and Elias Lindholm, unassisted, scored in the last eight minutes of the first. Nick Robertson got the Penguins back within 3-2 early in the second, then Zacha scored again, Morgan Geekie made it 5-2 and Fraser Minten added the sixth in the third. David Pastrnak and JJ Peterka each had two assists, both on Zacha's goals. Michael DiPietro only had to stop 16 of 18. At the other end, Arturs Silovs saw 24 shots and stopped 18, which is how you get to 5-9-2. The Bruins are 12-4-1. Pittsburgh's lead lasted three minutes and its defense never showed up, which is about how this season has gone for a franchise that keeps insisting it isn't rebuilding.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

DAL1CBJ2SOFinal: DAL 1, CBJ 2 SO

Two goalies, 65 minutes and one goal each, and Columbus won the skills competition. Cam Talbot and Casey DeSmith made it scoreless through two periods, and Mikko Rantanen's ninth, from Wyatt Johnston, looked like enough for Dallas midway through the third. Then Zach Werenski scored his first goal of the season with 3:14 left, from Kent Johnson and Matthew Knies, and the Blue Jackets never trailed again. In the shootout Valeri Nichushkin and Kent Johnson scored; Jason Robertson and Tyler Seguin didn't. Talbot finished with 27 saves on 28 shots plus both shootout attempts, and DeSmith stopped 29 of 30. Columbus is 7-7-0 with two straight wins. Dallas, without Miro Heiskanen, is 9-5-2. The Stars put one puck past Talbot in 65 minutes and none in the shootout, and that offense couldn't pass a referendum either.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

VAN2WPG6Final: VAN 2, WPG 6

Winnipeg went nine games without a win; now it has two in a row, and Vancouver was happy to help. Alex Iafallo scored on the power play at 3:49 and Cole Koepke added another 14 seconds later. Liam Ohgren answered for the Canucks, but Dawson Mercer scored his first of the season before the first intermission, Neal Pionk and Mark Scheifele scored in the second, and Mario Ferraro made it 6-1 in the third. Kyle Connor and Dylan DeMelo each had two assists, and Scheifele had a goal and an assist. Brock Boeser scored late. Stuart Skinner stopped 24 of 26 for the Jets, and Leevi Meriläinen gave up six on 29 shots. Winnipeg is 6-8-3. Vancouver is 3-14-1, the league's worst, and has become the team you play when you need to feel good about yourself again.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

ANA5EDM4Final: ANA 5, EDM 4

Pavel Mintyukov had the full Gordie Howe hat trick, and Anaheim held on in Edmonton, 5-4. Cutter Gauthier opened it on the power play, Evan Bouchard answered on one, and Connor McDavid scored shorthanded early in the second to make it 2-1 Oilers. Then the Ducks scored four straight: Mintyukov twice, his first two of the season, three minutes apart, and Beckett Sennecke twice, the second on the power play early in the third. Mintyukov also set up Sennecke's first and fought Kasperi Kapanen in the first period. Edmonton came back late: Kapanen on the power play, then Leon Draisaitl at 19:15 with the goalie pulled, but time ran out. McDavid had a goal and two assists. Laurent Brossoit stopped 23 of 27; Matt Tomkins 16 of 21. Edmonton is 11-3-3. Five goals on 21 shots: the Oilers' goaltending search goes on, now in its second decade.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

NSH3COL2OTFinal: NSH 3, COL 2 OT

Nashville goes past regulation again, and this time Steven Stamkos made it count. Ross Colton opened the scoring, Jaden Schwartz tied it, Vitali Pinchuk put the Predators back in front with his first of the season, and Parker Kelly tied it early in the second. After that, nothing for 37 minutes, until Stamkos scored on the power play 2:18 into overtime, from Roman Josi and Ryan O'Reilly. Justus Annunen was the story in the Nashville net, stopping 30 of 32 at Ball Arena, while Mackenzie Blackwood made 22 saves on 25 shots. Colorado tried a new top pair, with Sam Malinski beside Devon Toews and Cale Makar moved to Brett Kulak's side, and got two goals out of 32 shots for the trouble. The Predators are 7-4-5. The Avalanche, 9-6-2, have one of the league's best attacks and got outscored by Vitali Pinchuk and Ross Colton.

Thursday, November 5

Game recap

OTT2BUF1Final: OTT 2, BUF 1

Buffalo came home from a California sweep, led for most of the night, and still found a way to be Buffalo. Peyton Krebs put the Sabres up 1-0 at 14:00 of the second, his first of the season, off Tage Thompson and Zach Benson, and for a while Colten Ellis looked like he'd make it stand. Then the third period happened. Shane Pinto tied it at 11:33 from Philip Tomasino and Thomas Chabot, and Michael Amadio won it at 16:51 off Tim Stützle and Fabian Zetterlund: two goals in five minutes and change. Samuel Ersson stopped 23 of 24 for Ottawa, which had dropped three of four last week and needed this one. Ellis made 28 saves on 30 shots and deserved better. Ottawa is 10-6-1 and third in the Atlantic. Buffalo just learned that a one-goal lead in the third is only a rental, and Sabres fans have seen that lease run out before.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

CHI3FLA5Final: CHI 3, FLA 5

Sandis Vilmanis played 13 minutes and 32 seconds and put up four points, a night's work most top-six forwards would frame. The Panthers won 5-3: Vilmanis opened the scoring at 4:43, Carter Verhaeghe made it 2-0 on the power play and Seth Jones made it 3-0 in the second. Chicago, to its credit, made it interesting. Roman Kantserov got one back, Frank Nazar scored shorthanded and then again at 16:09 of the third to make it 4-3, with Connor Bedard assisting twice. But Vilmanis had already scored his second at 11:01, and Sam Reinhart's empty-netter at 18:33 closed it. Jacob Markstrom stopped 17 of 20; Spencer Knight made 25 saves on 29. Florida is 9-5-2 and 7-3-0 in its last 10. The Blackhawks are 4-11-1 and -27, which is a rebuild in the same way a house fire is a renovation.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

SJS2LAK7Final: SJS 2, LAK 7

Adrian Kempe walked back into the lineup and treated the Sharks like a practice dummy. Kempe scored 83 seconds in, again at 16:09 of the first, and completed the hat trick on a second-period power play, with an assist for a four-point night. Artemi Panarin had four assists, Quinton Byfield scored twice on the power play, and Erik Haula and Joel Armia piled on in a 7-2 Kings romp. Three of the seven came on the power play, which San Jose's penalty kill mostly watched. Macklin Celebrini and Ivar Stenberg scored for San Jose, both on the power play, but Yaroslav Askarov stopped just 20 of 27, and Darcy Kuemper made 30 saves on 32. The Kings are 5-7-2 and climbing out of their hole. The Sharks lost a third straight, their fifth in six, and held a players-only meeting afterward. Bring snacks, fellas: at this rate it's going to be a standing reservation.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

CGY1SEA2OTFinal: CGY 1, SEA 2 OT

Two goalies spent 60 minutes refusing to let anything happen, and then Matty Beniers decided he had somewhere to be. Beniers scored 55 seconds into overtime off Brandon Montour, and Seattle beat Calgary 2-1. Yegor Sharangovich opened the scoring at 12:45 of the first, and the Flames sat on that lead until Berkly Catton tied it at 13:09 of the second, stretching his point streak to seven games. After that it was Joey Daccord (25 saves on 26) and Dustin Wolf (27 on 29) trading stops until the 3-on-3 broke it open. Seattle is 9-5-1 and third in the Pacific. Calgary takes a point and is 7-8-1, scoring 2.44 goals a game, and the Saddledome goal horn is starting to wonder if it still has a job.

Wednesday, November 4

Game recap

UTA3TOR2Final: UTA 3, TOR 2

Jack Roslovic did everything a man can do in Toronto short of fixing the power play: two goals, both tying the game, both set up by Auston Matthews, and a point streak that's now seven games. Utah answered every time. Dylan Guenther scored on the power play with 13 seconds left in the first, Andrew Peeke snuck in the go-ahead goal in the second, and after Roslovic tied it again, Nick Schmaltz buried the winner on another Mammoth power play at 13:12 of the third. Clayton Keller ran the show with three assists, and Sebastian Cossa stopped 27 of 29. Sergei Bobrovsky made 33 saves on 36 shots for the Leafs, who went home with nothing but a long explanation of why they didn't challenge the second goal. Two power-play goals against, zero points: Toronto keeps finding new ways to lose in November so it doesn't have to wait for May.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

WPG5MTL4OTFinal: WPG 5, MTL 4 OT

Montreal led 4-0 with under three minutes to go, and the Jets' nine-game winless streak was about to become ten. Then it got weird. Tyrel Bauer, a defenseman with one goal to his name this season (that one), scored at 17:21, Morgan Barron at 18:03, and with Stuart Skinner on the bench Kyle Connor scored twice in 27 seconds, the tying goal on a power play with 33 seconds left. Four goals in 2:06. Dylan Samberg finished it 3:30 into overtime. Cole Caufield's two power-play goals and Owen Beck's first of the season went to waste, and Jacob Fowler faced 47 shots, which is about 20 more than anyone should. The Xhekaj brothers each found a dance partner in the third, Arber with Bauer and Florian with captain Adam Lowry. A five-game win streak ends and the Habs still get a point, but blowing a four-goal lead to a team that hadn't won since October is the kind of thing Leafs fans will be quoting back at them until spring.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

DET2TBL4Final: DET 2, TBL 4

Nikita Kucherov may be on his way out of Tampa, but he's still handing out goals on the way to the door. He set up both of Brayden Point's first-period goals, one on the power play, and Anthony Cirelli made it 3-0 midway through the second. John Gibson lasted one period (11 saves on 13 shots) before Daniil Tarasov took over and stopped 12 of 13. Lucas Raymond and J.T. Compher, on the power play early in the third, got Detroit within one, and then the Wings couldn't find the tying goal on the 21 shots Andrei Vasilevskiy saw all night. Ryan McDonagh scored his first of the season into the empty net with one second left, just to be thorough. The Lightning move to 9-3-2. Detroit's captain is suspended for refusing to play for them, the starter got the hook after 20 minutes, and the Red Wings' rebuild now needs a rebuild of its own.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

STL1NYR3Final: STL 1, NYR 3

With both of their regular goalies out, the Rangers handed the net to Dylan Garand, and Garand handed back 32 saves on 33 shots. That ended a four-game losing streak at the Garden, which had started to feel like a lease nobody could get out of. Adam Fox scored early in the second, Oliver Bjorkstrand made it 2-0 in the third, and Eeli Tolvanen hit the empty net at 17:59. Pius Suter ruined the shutout with 59 seconds left, the hockey version of taking the last slice of pizza when everybody's already full. Joel Hofer was good at the other end, 28 saves on 30, and the Blues have now been shut out or held to one goal in two of their last four games. They outshot New York 33-30 and lost by two, which is about as St. Louis as hockey gets: plenty of effort, nothing to show for it, and a long flight home to think about it.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

MIN4PHI2Final: MIN 4, PHI 2

The Wild scored twice in 31 seconds early in the first, Matt Boldy and then Michael McCarron, and Philadelphia spent the rest of the night chasing. Joel Eriksson Ek made it 3-0 42 seconds into the second. Tyson Foerster got one back, and Denver Barkey scored his first of the season on the power play early in the third to make it interesting, which in Philly counts as a comeback. Danila Yurov closed it with an empty-netter at 18:36. Jesper Wallstedt stopped 23 of 25, and Kirill Kaprizov and Quinn Hughes both pushed their point streaks to six games with assists. That's five straight road wins for Minnesota, now 11-3-3. Dan Vladar made 18 saves on 21 shots for the Flyers, who are 4-9-4 and still score the fewest goals in the league. Their best wingers are reportedly drawing interest from the team that just beat them, and at this rate the Flyers' front office might want to ask about Kaprizov instead.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

VGK3PIT2Final: VGK 3, PIT 2

Pittsburgh had a 2-1 lead halfway through the third and gave it away in the way only this version of the Penguins can. Tomas Hertl opened the scoring on a first-period power play, Tommy Novak and Rickard Rakell scored in the first ten minutes of the third, and then Trevor Connelly tied it at 11:19. With 35 seconds left, Hertl scored again on the power play, from Mark Stone and Jack Eichel. Ballgame. Adin Hill stopped 23 of 25 for Vegas, now 10-5-2; Arturs Silovs made 20 saves on 23 for the Penguins, who played without Evgeni Malkin and have lost two straight. Justin Brazeau made his season debut. A third-period lead, a power-play goal against and a loss: Pittsburgh's season in one shift, and the 2016 banners can't kill penalties.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

DAL6WSH5Final: DAL 6, WSH 5

Jason Robertson scored a natural hat trick in 5:20 at the start of the second period, the first on the power play, and Logan Thompson's night was over after 11 shots and four goals. That's how you get a 4-0 lead in Washington. Mikko Rantanen made it 5-1, and Roope Hintz made it 6-3 early in the third. Then the Capitals showed up: Jordan Kyrou, Boone Jenner and Jakob Chychrun (on a power play with 30 seconds left in the second) scored, and Justin Sourdif and Ryan Leonard, with the goalie pulled at 18:58, made it 6-5. Jake Oettinger, 20 saves on 25, held on for dear life. Charlie Lindgren stopped nine of 11 in relief. Dallas wins its second straight but loses Miro Heiskanen to an upper-body injury after one shift in the second. Washington scored five goals at home and lost, which is a lot of work for nothing, and its 5-1 home loss to Minnesota looks tidy by comparison.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

COL2CBJ7Final: COL 2, CBJ 7

Mathieu Olivier scored 28 seconds in and the Avalanche never caught up. Columbus put seven past two Colorado goalies: Scott Wedgewood was pulled after four goals on nine shots early in the second, and Mackenzie Blackwood didn't stop the bleeding either, 12 saves on 15. Charlie Coyle had two goals and two assists to tie his career high for points, Valeri Nichushkin scored against his old team, Ivan Provorov and Jake Christiansen got on the board from the back end, and Cole Sillinger added one. Cam Talbot made 27 saves on 29, allowing only a Cale Makar goal and a Nazem Kadri power-play goal. Afterward Jared Bednar called his team "hot, cold" and said he'd change how he spreads the ice time. The Blue Jackets end a two-game skid. The Avs came in averaging more than four goals a night and left having given up seven to the team that's played the fewest games in the league. Colorado's Cup window is letting in more than its goalies.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

EDM3NJD4SOFinal: EDM 3, NJD 4 SO

Jack Hughes scored twice in 45 seconds in the second, the second one on the power play, and the Devils led the league's best road team 3-1. Edmonton doesn't do quiet nights. Ryan Nugent-Hopkins scored on the power play with 1:44 left in the second, and Leon Draisaitl tied it on another power play one minute into the third. Overtime solved nothing, so it went to a shootout: Connor McDavid scored, Draisaitl didn't, and Jesper Bratt and Arseny Gritsyuk beat Tristan Jarry to win it. Hughes, of all people, missed his shot. Jarry was the better goalie on the night, 31 saves on 34, while Connor Hellebuyck made 18 on 21 and still won. Evan Bouchard opened the scoring in the first. The Oilers' perfect road record is gone, though they still collected a point. Edmonton gave up two power-play goals and lost a skills contest with McDavid on its side, which is the most Oilers sentence ever written.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

CAR1NSH4Final: CAR 1, NSH 4

The best team in the league walked into Nashville and ran into Juuse Saros, who stopped 29 of 30 and made Carolina look like the team in last place. Filip Forsberg set up the first two goals, Nick Perbix's first of the season in the first period and Roman Josi's early in the second. Jackson Blake got one back at 10:28 of the second, and that was all the Hurricanes got. Adam Edstrom restored the two-goal lead early in the third, and Ross Colton hit the empty net with 41 seconds left. Pyotr Kochetkov stopped 16 of 19. Carolina stays on 26 points, still the most in the league, after a team that's lost five times past regulation won one in 60 minutes for a change. The Canes outshot Nashville 30-20 and lost by three. Turns out shot share doesn't count in the standings, a lesson Carolina relearns every spring.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

ANA5VAN4Final: ANA 5, VAN 4

Cutter Gauthier scored a hat trick for the second straight game, two of the three on the power play, and Beckett Sennecke assisted on four of Anaheim's five goals. Mikael Granlund scored on the power play early and Leo Carlsson added a shorthanded one, which made it 3-1 and then 5-2 after Gauthier finished his hat trick 4:11 into the third. Vancouver didn't go quietly: Jake DeBrusk scored twice in four minutes, one on the power play, to make it 5-4 with 10 minutes left, but Laurent Brossoit held on with 19 saves on 23. Kevin Lankinen stopped 17 of 22. There were four fights, one of them a four-man scrap early in the third, and Jacob Quillan dropped the gloves twice. Anaheim has two straight wins. The Canucks are 3-13-1 and have lost three straight. Quillan had more fights last night than the Canucks have wins in their last four games.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Tuesday, November 3

Game recap

VGK2BOS3SOFinal: VGK 2, BOS 3 SO

Vegas spent two periods digging a hole at TD Garden, climbed all the way out, then forgot how to shoot a puck one-on-one. Rookie James Hagens opened the scoring in the first, his sixth of the year, and Morgan Geekie made it 2-0 on the power play early in the second. Braeden Bowman was ejected early in the second for elbowing Matthew Poitras, who didn't return. Mark Stone answered on a Vegas power play and Trevor Connelly tied it 7:23 into the third, with Mitch Marner setting up both for two assists. Overtime settled nothing, so it went to a shootout, where Connelly, Jack Eichel and Marner all came up empty against Jeremy Swayman (21 saves on 23 in regulation and OT) and David Pastrnak, after seven shots and no goal all night, finally found the net with Boston's last shooter. Carter Hart stopped 25 of 27 and got a loser's point for it. Boston moves to 11-4-1. Vegas goes to Pittsburgh tonight with three of the league's best hands, and not one of them could beat a goalie from 30 feet.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

DET5FLA3Final: DET 5, FLA 3

Detroit flew south and gave the two-time champs a lesson in finishing. Carter Mazur, playing all of 7:26, scored his first NHL goal in the first, and Sam Reinhart answered for Florida. Alex DeBrincat put the Wings back in front early in the second, then Aaron Ekblad tied it shorthanded, a goal so rare for him it was his first of the season. The third took 45 seconds to decide: Justin Faulk scored on the power play at 2:08 and Michael Brandsegg-Nygård followed at 2:53, adding seven hits for a two-point night. Sam Bennett made it 4-3 with Jacob Markstrom pulled, and Emmitt Finnie sealed it with an empty-netter three seconds from the end. Daniil Tarasov, starting against his old team, made 23 saves on 26 and Markstrom 24 on 28. Detroit goes to 7-5-3 and on to Tampa tonight. Florida dressed both Tkachuk brothers and still lost to a guy whose NHL goal total went from zero to one.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

COL5CHI2Final: COL 5, CHI 2

For about 15 minutes the United Center got to feel like it was 2013 again. Wyatt Kaiser scored 57 seconds in and Roman Kantserov made it 2-0 at 7:05 off a Connor Bedard feed. Then Colorado remembered it was Colorado. Nazem Kadri and Jaden Schwartz scored 26 seconds apart late in the first to tie it, Kadri added a power-play goal in the second off Cale Makar and Nathan MacKinnon, and Schwartz scored again with 11 seconds left in the period for two goals each. Devon Toews finished it into an empty net. Mackenzie Blackwood stopped 21 of 23 after the early hiccup, while Spencer Knight made 24 saves on 28. The Avalanche move to 9-5-1 and play in Columbus tonight. Chicago falls to 4-10-1: two goals up in seven minutes, five unanswered against, and the rebuild keeps finding new ways to lose.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

CGY2SJS1Final: CGY 2, SJS 1

Calgary won a game in San Jose with its depth forwards doing the scoring and Dustin Wolf doing everything else. Adam Klapka scored in the first off Jonathan Castagna, then set up William Stromgren's first of the season midway through the third, with Castagna on that one too. Neither of them played 12 minutes, and they still outscored the Sharks' whole top six. Sam Dickinson got San Jose on the board less than three minutes later, but Wolf, who made 26 saves on 27, shut the door from there. Yaroslav Askarov was solid at the other end with 20 saves on 22. The Flames improve to 7-8-0. The Sharks drop to 7-8-1 with a fourth loss in five games, and Dickinson admitted there's frustration in the room. When your best chance is a defenseman's first goal of the year and the other team's grinders are running the show, the frustration makes sense.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Monday, November 2

Game recap

WPG0CAR7Final: WPG 0, CAR 7

Carolina hosted Winnipeg on Sunday and ran it like a practice with fans. Sean Walker opened the scoring shorthanded at 5:16 of the first, and then the Hurricanes put up four goals in 7:14 of the second: Juuso Välimäki, Sebastian Aho on the power play, Walker again, and Logan Stankoven for his 10th. Stuart Skinner was pulled after 12 saves on 17 shots, and Clay Stevenson gave up two more in the third to Mark Jankowski (power play) and Jesperi Kotkaniemi. At the other end, Pyotr Kochetkov had a quiet night: 26 saves and a shutout. Carolina is 12-2-2 with 26 points, the most in the league. Winnipeg is 0-7-2 in its last nine, and the hot seat in that building is starting to need its own Zamboni.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

MIN5WSH1Final: MIN 5, WSH 1

Minnesota came into Washington without Brock Faber or Jared Spurgeon and still treated the Capitals like the undercard. Quinn Hughes scored 3:42 in, Michael McCarron added another 1:45 later, and the Wild sat on 2-0 until Justin Sourdif got one back with six seconds left in the second. That was all Washington got off Jesper Wallstedt, who stopped 26 of 27. Then the third turned into a fire sale: Maxim Shabanov scored on the power play, Kirill Kaprizov hit the empty net for his 15th of the season, and Danila Yurov added another power-play goal with 25 seconds left. Logan Thompson made 24 saves on 28 shots. The Wild are 10-3-3 and first in the Central. Washington's offense showed up for six seconds, so maybe that Larkin phone call to Detroit should go out sooner rather than later.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

UTA3PHI6Final: UTA 3, PHI 6

Travis Konecny came back from 10 games on IR and the league's lowest-scoring team suddenly found six. Matvei Michkov opened it with his 10th, Dmitri Simashev answered for Utah, and Konecny scored his first of the season 1:06 into the second. Noah Cates, Christian Dvorak and Oliver Bonk made it 5-1 by 5:35 of the third. Utah's power play woke up late, with Mikhail Sergachev scoring and then Logan Cooley with the goalie pulled, before Cole Knuble iced it into the empty net. Lawson Crouse and Simon Benoit fought in the third. Dan Vladar made 19 saves, and Karel Vejmelka stopped 15 of 20. Utah gave up five goals on 20 shots to the team that scores the fewest in the league, which is a bit like losing a footrace to a guy carrying a couch.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

EDM4NYR1Final: EDM 4, NYR 1

Connor McDavid scored 50 seconds in, and the Rangers spent the rest of the night chasing the bus. Evan Bouchard set up McDavid and Colton Dach in the opening 6:19, then scored on the power play in the second. His goal and two assists make him the fourth defenseman with 25 or more points through a season's first 15 games, alongside Bobby Orr, Al MacInnis and Denis Potvin. Pavel Dorofeyev scored for New York, and Dach hit the empty net for his first multigoal NHL game. Matt Tomkins won his Oilers debut with 27 saves on 28 shots; Dylan Garand made 21. Edmonton is 11-2-2 and 7-0-0 on the road, and McDavid has 39 points. The Rangers have lost four straight, and the Garden crowd is now paying Broadway prices for a show that closes in the first act.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

OTT3ANA6Final: OTT 3, ANA 6

Ottawa led 3-0 after one period in Anaheim and then forgot there were two more. Philip Tomasino, Claude Giroux and Michael Amadio scored in the first, but Cutter Gauthier and Judd Caulfield cut it to 3-2 early in the second, and Caulfield tied it on the power play with 42 seconds left in the period. The third was a power-play clinic: Gauthier scored twice in 36 seconds to finish a hat trick, and Roger McQueen added a fourth power-play goal for the night. Leo Carlsson had three assists. Dylan Cozens was ejected after a long video review for a blindside hit on A.J. Greer. Laurent Brossoit made 19 saves on 22 shots, and Jonas Johansson stopped 27 of 33. Blowing a three-goal lead on the road isn't a collapse in Ottawa, it's a franchise tradition with a logo.

Sunday, November 1

Game recap

CHI4BOS5OTFinal: CHI 4, BOS 5 OT

Chicago did almost everything right in Boston, which for the Blackhawks is the most dangerous place to be. Anton Frondell scored twice on nine shots, Connor Bedard made it 4-2 at 12:20 of the third, and the Hawks outshot the Bruins 41-32. Then the wheels came off, right on schedule. Mason Lohrei answered 46 seconds after Bedard, Morgan Geekie tied it with 12 seconds left and Michael DiPietro on the bench, and Elias Lindholm ended it 2:32 into overtime off a Charlie McAvoy feed. McAvoy and JJ Peterka had two assists each, DiPietro made 37 saves, and Nikita Zadorov somehow piled up 14 penalty minutes without a fight. Arvid Soderblom stopped 27 of 32. Boston is 10-4-1. Chicago is 4-9-1 and has perfected the two-goal lead with eight minutes left: the rebuild comes with a free lesson every night.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

STL5DET4Final: STL 5, DET 4

Detroit led St. Louis 4-2 early in the third, at home, with the Blues managing all of 15 shots on the night. That should be a win. It was not. Pavel Buchnevich cut it to 4-3 at 8:37, Justin Barron tied it at 12:57, and 18 seconds later Aleksanteri Kaskimaki scored his first of the season to finish a three-goal burst in 4:38. John Gibson saw 15 shots and let in five, a .667 save percentage Red Wings fans will see in their sleep. Lucas Raymond had a goal and an assist, Emmitt Finnie scored on the power play, and Keegan Kolesar and J.T. Compher got their first goals of the season. Jimmy Snuggerud and Barron had two points each for St. Louis, and Joel Hofer stopped 24 of 28. The Blues are 7-6-1. Detroit is 6-5-3 and has found a way to make 15 shots feel like a barrage.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

TBL4NSH5SOFinal: TBL 4, NSH 5 SO

Tampa Bay and Nashville traded goals for 60 minutes like two teams that had never heard of defense, then went to a shootout where nobody could score at all. Seven straight shooters missed before Steven Stamkos beat Andrei Vasilevskiy, and Gage Goncalves missed to end it. Stamkos had already tied it 4-4 on the power play at 7:27 of the third. Nikita Kucherov had three assists, John Carlson had a goal and an assist, and Jake Guentzel, Victor Hedman and Conor Geekie also scored for Tampa Bay. Jayden Struble's goal with 18 seconds left in the second kept Nashville level, and Filip Forsberg and Nick Perbix had two assists each. Justus Annunen made 22 saves on 26 shots; Vasilevskiy stopped 29 of 33. Nashville is 5-4-5. Tampa Bay is 8-3-2 and still hasn't figured out that the guy who spent 16 seasons scoring for them knows exactly where to shoot on Vasilevskiy.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

EDM4NYI0Final: EDM 4, NYI 0

Edmonton showed up on Long Island and treated the Islanders like an optional skate. Tristan Jarry stopped all 18 shots for the shutout, which tells you how much the Isles generated: 18 shots in 60 minutes, on home ice. Ryan Nugent-Hopkins scored twice, the second on a power play set up by Connor McDavid and Leon Draisaitl, and Vasily Podkolzin got his ninth of the year 68 seconds after the opener. Draisaitl had two assists, and Jason Dickinson put it in the empty net late. Ilya Sorokin made 20 saves on 23 shots and deserved better, which at this point is the Islanders goalie's job description. Edmonton is 10-2-2. New York is 7-5-2, and if 18 shots is the plan, Sorokin should start billing them by the hour.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

BUF3LAK2Final: BUF 3, LAK 2

Buffalo went to Los Angeles and won a hockey game, which is still news. Jack Quinn opened the scoring on the power play, Tage Thompson made it 2-0 late in the second, and after the Kings tied it on a Corey Perry power-play goal and Andre Lee's first of the year early in the third, Thompson won it on another power play at 13:40. That's two for Thompson, now at 10 goals, plus an assist for Quinn and two each for Rasmus Dahlin and Zach Benson. Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen stopped 27 of 29. Anton Forsberg made 28 saves for LA. The Sabres are 7-4-3. The Kings are 4-7-2, and their 41-year-old power-play scorer is the only thing in the building that looks like 2012.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

OTT5SJS1Final: OTT 5, SJS 1

Ottawa came into San Jose and politely took the Sharks apart. Dylan Cozens opened it, Michael Misa answered, and then the Senators scored three times in 7:13 of the second: Drake Batherson, Tim Stützle, and a short-handed goal from Ridly Greig. Shane Pinto, who set up Greig, added the empty-netter. Jake Sanderson had two assists, and Samuel Ersson stopped 22 of 23 to make Misa's goal the only blemish. Ottawa outshot San Jose 35-23. Alex Nedeljkovic made 30 saves and could have used some help from the five guys in front of him. Ottawa is 9-5-1. San Jose is 7-7-1, and when the other team's penalty kill outscores your power play, the rebuild has a few chapters left.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

PIT4MTL5Final: PIT 4, MTL 5

Montreal and Pittsburgh scored six goals in the first 22 minutes and 21 seconds, the hockey version of a food fight. Erik Karlsson scored on the power play at 2:08, Oliver Kapanen and Josh Anderson answered within a minute, and by the time Chris Kreider made it 4-2 early in the second the goalies were looking for the exits. Anderson scored twice, Lane Hutson had two assists, and Owen Beck dropped the gloves with Blake Lizotte. Sidney Crosby had a goal and two assists, passing Ray Bourque for the most assists with one franchise and tying Marcel Dionne for sixth in career points; his 6-on-5 goal at 16:49 of the third made it close. Jacob Fowler stopped 25 of 29. Sergei Murashov made 22 saves on 27 shots and is 0-4-1. Montreal is 9-3-2. Pittsburgh is 5-7-2, and Crosby's milestones are the only highlight package left.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

TOR4VAN2Final: TOR 4, VAN 2

Vancouver keeps finding new ways to lose, and Toronto was happy to help. William Nylander scored 83 seconds in, Brock Boeser tied it on the power play, and then Auston Matthews (his 11th) and Zack MacEwen, of all people, put the Leafs up 3-1 in the second. Max Sasson made it 3-2 midway through the third before Teddy Blueger iced it into the empty net, with Anthony Stolarz picking up the assist. Stolarz made 26 saves on 28 shots. Leevi Meriläinen stopped 24 of 27. Toronto is 8-6-2. Vancouver is 3-12-1 with seven points in 16 games, and the only thing the Canucks finish these days is the third period.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

CBJ1DAL3Final: CBJ 1, DAL 3

Dallas won this one on 17 shots, which is either efficient or a cry for help. Mikko Rantanen scored on the power play 2:16 in, Thomas Harley got his first of the season with one second left in the first, and Jake Oettinger did the rest, stopping 24 of 25. Damon Severson broke the shutout at 6:21 of the third, but Arttu Hyry hit the empty net with one second left, because apparently Dallas only scores at the buzzer. Miro Heiskanen had two assists. Jet Greaves stopped 14 of 16 and outplayed the skaters in front of him. Dallas is 8-5-1. Columbus is 5-7-0 and outshot the Stars 25-17 for its trouble, proof the Blue Jackets can control a game for 60 minutes and still find a way to lose it.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

CGY2COL5Final: CGY 2, COL 5

Calgary walked into Ball Arena and got politely escorted out. Nathan MacKinnon opened the scoring, Martin Necas added a power-play goal, and Artturi Lehkonen and Brock Nelson scored 3:19 apart in the second to make it 4-0 before the Flames found their skates. Cale Makar had four assists, MacKinnon had a goal and an assist, and Lehkonen scored twice to reach 12 goals. Joel Farabee and Martin Pospisil got it to 4-2, then Lehkonen ended any thought of a comeback 2:10 later. Mackenzie Blackwood stopped 25 of 27; Arsenii Sergeev made 29 saves on 34 shots. Colorado is 8-5-1. Calgary is 6-8-0, and the Flames' idea of a push is two goals once they're down four.

Saturday, October 31

Game recap

NJD5VGK2Final: NJD 5, VGK 2

Vegas went up 2-1 late in the first, Mitch Marner setting up Mark Stone on the power play and Ivan Barbashev a minute later, and then the Golden Knights apparently checked out of the hotel early. Arseny Gritsyuk tied it alone with 69 seconds left in the period, Jack Hughes put New Jersey ahead 3:49 into the second, and Gritsyuk buried his second with under two minutes left in the middle frame. Hughes added an empty-netter for two of his own, Luke Hughes chipped in a goal, and the Devils won 5-2 to get to 9-5-0. Gritsyuk fired eight shots, Hughes seven. Connor Hellebuyck stopped 19 of 21; Adin Hill made 27 saves on 31. Jack Eichel finished with no points and no shots in 16 minutes, a quiet night for the man whose name is on the marquee. Vegas came in built to go all in and left with exactly what the house usually leaves you: nothing.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

WPG2FLA5Final: WPG 2, FLA 5

Anton Lundell came into the night with one goal this season and left with four, a hat trick on eight shots as Florida beat Winnipeg 5-2 for its third straight win. Sam Reinhart opened the scoring on the power play late in the first, Lundell made it 2-0 early in the second, and after Kyle Connor answered on a Jets power play, Seth Jones restored the two-goal cushion with another Panthers power-play goal. Morgan Barron scored his first of the year to make it 3-2 midway through the third, which only seemed to annoy Lundell, who scored at 13:33 and then into the empty net. Jones finished with a goal and two assists. Akira Schmid stopped 22 of 24; Nico Daws faced 37 shots and made 33 saves, which is about all you can ask of a man playing behind this. Bokondji Imama and Tyrel Bauer dropped the gloves 2:04 in. Winnipeg is 1-7-2 in its last 10, and the Jets' four-game skid now has the shelf life of a Winnipeg winter: long, dark and nowhere near done.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

SEA2CGY6Final: SEA 2, CGY 6

Calgary scored six goals in a game, which in this town counts as a civic holiday. The Flames beat Seattle 6-2 behind Matt Coronato's four points (a goal and three assists) and Joel Farabee's three, with Morgan Frost and Matvei Gridin each adding a goal and an assist. Frost opened it on the power play 2:32 in, Frederick Gaudreau tied it, and then the second period turned into a Flames clinic: Aydar Suniev, Gridin on another power play and Farabee made it 4-1 inside five minutes. That was the end of Philipp Grubauer's night, four goals on 14 shots; Joey Daccord stopped 11 of 13 in relief. Mackie Samoskevich got one back on a Kraken power play, but Coronato scored 39 seconds into the third and Ryan Strome added the sixth. Dustin Wolf made 20 saves on 22, and Adam Klapka and Curtis Douglas fought 1:46 in. Seattle brought two goalies and still couldn't find one who'd close the door.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Friday, October 30

Game recap

WPG4TBL6Final: WPG 4, TBL 6

Tampa Bay 6, Winnipeg 4, and the 4 is doing a lot of lying. The Lightning blew this open with three goals in the last 4:04 of the second period, John Carlson and Brandon Hagel 56 seconds apart, and it was 5-1 before the Jets remembered they had a game to play. Pontus Holmberg went 1-3-4, Anthony Cirelli added a power-play goal and three points, and Brayden Point opened the scoring 2:20 in off a Kucherov feed. Stuart Skinner stopped 16 of 21 and got the hook after 40 minutes; Nico Daws stopped all nine he saw in relief. Neal Pionk scored twice, Mark Scheifele had three assists, and Kyle Connor's 10th of the year with the goalie pulled made it 5-4 with 2:48 left. Holmberg's empty-netter ended it. The Jets keep losing their games and finding them again in the third, which is like reporting your wallet stolen after you've already spent everything in it.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

UTA4PIT3OTFinal: UTA 4, PIT 3 OT

Logan Cooley scored a hat trick, and the third one came with one second left in regulation, which is the hockey equivalent of catching the last train as the doors close on your coat. Cooley had Utah up 2-0 in the first period, then Pittsburgh crawled back: Erik Karlsson in the second, Rickard Rakell shorthanded in the third, and Ben Kindel with 25 seconds left to make it 3-2 Penguins. Utah pulled Sebastian Cossa, Cooley buried the 6-on-5 tying goal at 19:59, and Mikhail Sergachev ended it 3:27 into overtime off a Barrett Hayton feed. Cossa made 31 saves on 34 shots; Arturs Silovs stopped 30 of 34. Evgeni Malkin had two assists in a game Pittsburgh had won for exactly 24 seconds. Utah goes to 9-5-0. The Penguins go home with one point and the lingering feeling that the clock in Pittsburgh runs a little slow.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

CBJ2CAR3Final: CBJ 2, CAR 3

Carolina built a 3-0 lead, took its foot off the gas for about three minutes, and still won 3-2, because that's how life goes when you're 11-2-2 with 24 points. Jordan Martinook scored in the first, Logan Stankoven got his ninth in the second, and Mark Jankowski scored 16 seconds into the third, with Seth Jarvis setting up two of them. Columbus woke up when Denton Mateychuk scored at 6:56 of the third and Kent Johnson added a power-play goal under three minutes later, then spent the last 10 minutes discovering why nobody comes back on the Hurricanes. Pyotr Kochetkov made 24 saves on 26 shots; Jet Greaves stopped 24 of 27. The Blue Jackets fall to 5-6-0, a team that plays its best hockey once the scoreboard has already filed its report.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

CHI1DET4Final: CHI 1, DET 4

With Dylan Larkin's trade request hanging over the building, Viktor Arvidsson decided Detroit could use somebody who actually wants to score for it. Arvidsson had a hat trick, the last one into an empty net, and the Red Wings beat Chicago 4-1. Connor Bedard gave the Blackhawks a 1-0 lead 5:59 in, which they protected for a full period and change before Arvidsson tied it in the second. Lucas Raymond scored on the power play 69 seconds into the third, Arvidsson made it 3-1 at 15:26 and finished the hat trick 79 seconds later. Alex DeBrincat had two assists. John Gibson stopped 18 of 19 on a light night; Spencer Knight made 27 saves on 30 shots for Chicago, which drops to 4-9-0. The Blackhawks have Bedard and a plan, and as of this morning the plan is still mostly Bedard.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

BOS1STL4Final: BOS 1, STL 4

Boston came to St. Louis at 9-3-1 and left with a 4-1 loss and a Joel Hofer problem. Hofer stopped 31 of 32, and the only one he missed was James Hagens' fifth of the season 5:28 in. After that it was all Blues: Jimmy Snuggerud tied it on the power play, Philip Broberg put them ahead early in the second, Robert Thomas made it 3-1, and Jake Neighbours added another power-play goal in the third. Broberg and Thomas each had a goal and two assists. Jeremy Swayman stopped 14 of 18, which is not the number you want when your team gives up 18 shots all night. The Bruins are 9-4-1 and still fine, but they found out St. Louis has a power play, and that their penalty kill left the door unlocked.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

WSH4NSH3Final: WSH 4, NSH 3

Nashville tied this game three times and lost it anyway, which is a pretty good summary of the Predators' season. Washington won 4-3 in Nashville behind two goals from Cole Hutson, who answered Filip Forsberg's first-period power-play goal and later put the Capitals ahead 3-2 in the second. Boone Jenner scored in between. Forsberg scored twice and Roman Josi had three assists, and Ross Colton tied it 3-3 at 6:34 of the third, before Alex Tuch scored his 10th of the season at 10:09 to win it. Charlie Lindgren made 24 saves on 27 shots; Juuse Saros stopped 25 of 29. Washington goes to 8-4-0. The Predators are 4-4-5, and five overtime-or-shootout losses in 13 games means they've mastered the art of being almost good enough.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

MTL5DAL2Final: MTL 5, DAL 2

Montreal went to Dallas without Nick Suzuki and came home with a 5-2 win, so maybe the Canadiens should lend some of that depth to the rest of the league. Cole Caufield scored twice in the first, his seventh and eighth of the season, and Alex Newhook added two of his own, including the one that made it 4-1 early in the second. Noah Dobson had two assists. Wyatt Johnston scored on the power play and Jamie Benn added one for Dallas, but that's as close as the Stars got, and Phillip Danault's empty-netter with 48 seconds left was his first goal of the year. Jakub Dobes stopped 17 of 19; Jake Oettinger allowed four on 20 shots. The Habs go to 8-3-2. Dallas is 7-5-1 and has now lost two straight, which in Texas is a crisis.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

NYI4MIN3OTFinal: NYI 4, MIN 3 OT

Joel Eriksson Ek scored 27 seconds in, and Matthew Schaefer scored 33 seconds into overtime, so the Islanders won 4-3 in a game that started and ended before you could find the remote. Schaefer had two goals and an assist, Bo Horvat scored on the power play, and Adam Pelech scored his first of the season to make it 3-2 midway through the third. Quinn Hughes, still the most-discussed player in the league, scored for Minnesota, and Matt Boldy tied it unassisted at 16:07 of the third. Jean-Gabriel Pageau set up the winner. Ilya Sorokin made 22 saves on 25 shots; Jesper Wallstedt stopped 22 of 26. Minnesota is 9-3-3 and still gets a point, but the Wild just keep running into overtime like it's a puddle they can't help stepping in.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

BUF7ANA6Final: BUF 7, ANA 6

Thirteen goals, and the goalies get to share the blame. Buffalo won 7-6 in Anaheim after falling behind 2-0 on two Ducks power-play goals in the first three minutes and 3-1 at 10:38. Then Tage Thompson took over: he tied it 3-3 in the first and scored twice in 15 seconds late in the second, 18:36 and 18:51, for a hat trick. Jack Quinn and Zach Benson made it 7-3 early in the third, and the Sabres went to sleep. Cutter Gauthier scored his second power-play goal, then Tristan Luneau and Beckett Sennecke scored with Anaheim's net empty in the last 68 seconds, and the Sabres held on for dear life. Peyton Krebs had three assists. Colten Ellis stopped 29 of 35; Ville Husso allowed seven on 30 shots. The Ducks drop to 5-7-1, proof that a late comeback works better when you start it before you're down four.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

OTT5LAK6OTFinal: OTT 5, LAK 6 OT

Los Angeles led 5-1 in the second period and still needed overtime, and Quinton Byfield had to bail them out 3:37 into it. Ottawa's Tyler Kleven scored first, then the Kings rattled off five: Erik Haula on the power play, Trevor Moore, Mikey Anderson, Joel Armia 37 seconds later to chase Jonas Johansson, and Artemi Panarin on the power play. The game got ugly in the second, when Hayden Hodgson was thrown out for a hit to Brandt Clarke's head and Nick Cousins was also ejected. Then the Senators came back: Dylan Cozens scored twice, Drake Batherson added a goal and two assists, and Shane Pinto tied it 5-5 with the goalie pulled at 18:20. Drew Doughty had three assists, Darcy Kuemper stopped 17 of 22, and Samuel Ersson stopped 20 of 22 in relief. The Kings go to 4-6-2, with a defense that treats a four-goal lead like a security deposit it never expects to get back.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

VAN2SJS3Final: VAN 2, SJS 3

Vancouver led 2-0 going into the third period in San Jose, and you already know how this ends. Drew O'Connor scored in the first and Liam Ohgren made it 2-0 with 64 seconds left in the second. Then the Sharks scored three times in 2:50: Will Smith on the power play at 8:00, Smith again at 10:39 off a Macklin Celebrini feed, and Mason Marchment 11 seconds after that. Yaroslav Askarov made 23 saves on 25 shots, and Leevi Meriläinen stopped 21 of 24 for the Canucks. San Jose goes to 7-6-1. Vancouver falls to 3-11-1, a team so used to losing that it now gets its two-goal leads out of the way early so it has more time to give them back.

Thursday, October 29

Game recap

PHI2WSH5Final: PHI 2, WSH 5

Dylan Strome handed out treats a few days early: three assists, all of them gift-wrapped for Alex Tuch and Jordan Kyrou in a 5-2 Capitals win over Philadelphia. Tuch opened the scoring 1:50 in and closed it with an empty-netter, two goals on the night. Kyrou also scored twice, a power-play goal in the second and the one that put Washington back up two after Matvei Michkov's power-play goal made it 3-2 midway through the third. Sean Couturier had the other Flyers goal, and Aliaksei Protas got his first of the season. Logan Thompson stopped 23 of 25; Joseph Woll stopped 25 of 29. Matt Roy threw nine hits and still found time for an assist. Washington is 7-4-0. Philadelphia is 3-8-4, and two goals is starting to look less like a bad night and more like the ceiling.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

CGY0EDM4Final: CGY 0, EDM 4

The Battle of Alberta lasted about one period. Mathieu Joseph scored at 7:46 of the first off a Connor McDavid feed, Mattias Ekholm made it 2-0 in the second, and then Edmonton scored twice in 21 seconds early in the third: Kasperi Kapanen on the power play and Alex Formenton right behind him. McDavid and Ryan Nugent-Hopkins had two assists each, and Tristan Jarry stopped all 24 shots for the shutout. Calgary tried a goalie change after the first, with Devin Cooley (8 saves on 9) giving way to Dustin Wolf (20 on 23), which fixed nothing because the problem was at the other end. Ty Emberson and Brennan Othmann dropped the gloves in the first. Edmonton is 9-2-2. Calgary is 5-7-0 and used two goalies and zero goals, which is a lot of equipment for a night with nothing to show for it.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

NJD2COL5Final: NJD 2, COL 5

Connor Brown scored both New Jersey goals, including an unassisted shorthanded one in the first, and the Devils still got run over 5-2 in Denver. Colorado scored five straight: Gabriel Landeskog tied it on the power play in the second, then Nazem Kadri, Parker Kelly, Nathan MacKinnon and Jaden Schwartz piled on in the third, the last two 30 seconds apart. Brent Burns and Sam Malinski had two assists each, and Kadri and Schwartz had a goal and an assist. The Avalanche outshot New Jersey 44-22; Jake Allen made 39 saves, Mackenzie Blackwood 20. Colorado is 7-5-1. New Jersey is 8-5-0, and after trading for a Vezina goalie last week, the 44 shots suggest the next phone call should be about the defense.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

TOR4SEA5Final: TOR 4, SEA 5

Toronto did the hard part and then forgot to finish. Down 4-2 in the third, the Leafs got one from Jack Roslovic and a 6-on-5 tying goal from Auston Matthews with 1:30 left, and then Brandon Montour won it for Seattle with 33 seconds to go, 5-4. Gavin McKenna had his first two-goal game, both on the power play, plus an assist; Matthews had a goal and two assists. Seattle spread it around: Berkly Catton, Josh Mahura with his first of the season, Chandler Stephenson on the power play, Ryker Evans and Montour, with Mackie Samoskevich adding two assists. Sergei Bobrovsky stopped 12 of 17; Philipp Grubauer 18 of 22. Cale Fleury and Vinni Lettieri fought in the second. Seattle is 8-4-1. Toronto is 7-6-2 and erased a two-goal deficit only to lose in the last minute, which is the most Maple Leafs sentence ever written.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Wednesday, October 28

Game recap

CBJ4PHI3OTFinal: CBJ 4, PHI 3 OT

Columbus scored three goals in 2:46 of the first period, then spent the next 40 minutes trying to give them back, and the Flyers almost took the gift. Adam Fantilli, Kent Johnson and Denton Mateychuk built the 3-0 lead on a Dan Vladar who finished with 11 saves on 15 shots, which is a lot of goals for a team that only managed 15 shots all night. Noah Cates and Trevor Zegras chipped away, and Jamie Drysdale tied it with the goalie pulled and 11 seconds left. Then Johnson, with two goals and an assist, ended it 2:22 into overtime. Cam Talbot made 28 saves for the Blue Jackets. Philadelphia outshot Columbus 31-15 and still lost, now 0-3 in 3-on-3 overtime, the hockey version of running a marathon and missing the finish line by a step. The Flyers keep finding new ways to lose, and they're getting creative about it.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

BOS1CAR2Final: BOS 1, CAR 2

The Bruins scored 91 seconds in, on a Pavel Zacha power-play goal, and then apparently decided that was plenty. Boston managed 15 shots all night. Carolina had 30, and Jeremy Swayman (28 saves) kept it close until the Hurricanes finally solved him. Jackson Blake tied it with 52 seconds left in the first, and Sebastian Aho put home his eighth of the season at 10:19 of the third for the winner. Pyotr Kochetkov needed only 14 saves, which is basically a paid night off. Nicolas Deslauriers and Tanner Jeannot dropped the gloves in the first for the evening's other entertainment, and Mark Jankowski returned to the Carolina lineup. The Hurricanes move to 10-2-2. The Bruins are 9-3-1 and still good, but 15 shots against a top team is a business trip where you forget your laptop.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

LAK1CHI2Final: LAK 1, CHI 2

Chicago snapped a three-game losing streak, and it took a defenseman scoring his first of the year to do it. Samuel Helenius gave the Kings an early lead with his first goal of the season at 2:31, and Los Angeles then went the final 57 minutes without another one. Roman Kantserov tied it on a second-period power play off a Connor Bedard feed, and Wyatt Kaiser won it at 7:17 of the third, from Frank Nazar and Patrick Kane. Spencer Knight was excellent with 25 saves on 26 shots; Anton Forsberg made 25 at the other end. Quinton Byfield fired six shots and Artemi Panarin played nearly 24 minutes without a point. The Blackhawks improve to 4-8-0. The Kings fall to 3-6-2 with one goal from their fourth line and none from anybody paid to score them.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

MTL2STL0Final: MTL 2, STL 0

Jacob Fowler stopped all 46 shots the Blues threw at him, and St. Louis threw just about everything, the rink's spare pucks included. Philip Broberg had six shots, four other Blues had five each, and none of them got one past Fowler. The Canadiens needed only 20 shots of their own. Zachary Bolduc scored in the second period, Florian Xhekaj got his first of the season early in the third, and Mike Matheson assisted on both. Jordan Binnington made 18 saves and still took the loss, which won't help a goalie already sitting on the trade boards. Montreal is 7-3-2. The Blues fall to 5-6-1 after outshooting a team 46-20 and getting shut out, and at some point they have to stop blaming the goalie and start blaming the aim.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

NYI4NSH3SOFinal: NYI 4, NSH 3 SO

The Islanders led 3-0 eight minutes into the second period, and Nashville spent the rest of regulation proving that no lead in Music City is safe. Anthony Duclair, Brayden Schenn and Bo Horvat built it; Filip Forsberg (power play), Alexander Kerfoot and Ryan O'Reilly erased it, O'Reilly tying the game 4:16 into the third. Overtime solved nothing, though Matthew Schaefer played all of it and finished with 32:16 of ice time, the kind of workload usually reserved for a veteran. In the shootout Kyle Palmieri and Horvat scored, while O'Reilly and Forsberg both missed. Semyon Varlamov made 20 saves; Juuse Saros made 25. New York is 6-4-2. The Predators are 4-3-5, a team so committed to the loser point it should hang a banner for it.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

NJD5DAL1Final: NJD 5, DAL 1

Connor Hellebuyck's Devils debut was about as stressful as a warm bath: 17 saves on 18 shots, with the skaters in front of him doing everything else. Nico Hischier scored twice, opening the night at 2:41 and adding another 38 seconds into the second. Jesper Boqvist, Luke Hughes and Jack Hughes did the rest, and the Hughes brothers each had a goal. Justin Hryckowian got Dallas its only goal. Jamie Benn and Brenden Dillon fought in the second period, which was the closest the Stars came to winning anything. Casey DeSmith allowed five goals on 27 shots. New Jersey has won four straight and is 8-4-0. Dallas falls to 7-4-1 and looked like a team that had read about Hellebuyck all week and decided not to bother him.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

FLA5WPG1Final: FLA 5, WPG 1

Florida was up 3-0 before the 11-minute mark, and Winnipeg's penalty kill treated the Panthers' power play like a guest of honour. Carter Verhaeghe scored twice on the power play, Niko Mikkola added one in between, and Sam Reinhart made it three power-play goals on the night in the second. Brady Tkachuk finished it in the third, with brother Matthew assisting for his fourth helper of the night. Seth Jones had three assists. Adam Lowry's shorthanded goal was the only thing Jets fans got to cheer. Akira Schmid made 24 saves; Clay Stevenson allowed five on 24 shots. The Panthers are 7-4-2. The Jets are 4-5-3, and a penalty kill that leaky makes every Florida trip to the box look like a free shift.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

MIN3UTA1Final: MIN 3, UTA 1

Three fights and two power-play goals: the Wild brought both the fists and the finish to Utah. Liam O'Brien and Michael McCarron fought in the first, Mikhail Sergachev and Matt Boldy went 88 seconds later, and Vincent Trocheck and Danila Yurov added a third in the second. When the hockey broke out, Minnesota's power play did the damage. Joel Eriksson Ek scored in the second and Kirill Kaprizov got his 14th of the season 48 seconds into the third, both with Quinn Hughes assisting. Maxim Shabanov made it 3-0, and Logan Cooley's late 6-on-5 goal only spoiled the shutout. Jesper Wallstedt made 26 saves; Karel Vejmelka made 27. The Wild are 9-3-2. Utah is 8-5-0 and learned that winning the fights doesn't count on the scoreboard.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

OTT1VGK4Final: OTT 1, VGK 4

For almost 40 minutes nobody scored; then Vegas remembered it's the house. Braeden Bowman scored on the power play with 11 seconds left in the second, Shane Pinto answered on a power play 34 seconds into the third, and Raphael Lavoie scored his first of the season at 8:01 for the winner. William Karlsson and Jack Eichel then added empty-netters, which turns a nervy 2-1 into a 4-1 final. Adin Hill was sharp with 25 saves on 26 shots, and Jonas Johansson matched him with 25 of 27 before the empty net did the rest. Mitch Marner had an assist on Karlsson's goal. Vegas is 9-4-1. The Senators fall to 8-5-0 and flew all that way to learn the Vegas lesson: you can stay at the table a long time, but you don't walk out ahead.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

VAN6ANA5OTFinal: VAN 6, ANA 5 OT

The Canucks hadn't won in double-digit games, trailed 5-2 with under eight minutes left, and somehow won. Anaheim had this one framed: A.J. Greer scored twice, Jeff Malott, Beckett Sennecke and Leo Carlsson piled on, and it was 4-1 after two. Then Brock Boeser and Jamie Oleksiak scored, and Jonathan Lekkerimäki scored twice with the goalie pulled, at 17:14 and 18:03, to tie it. Filip Hronek won it on a power play 4:49 into overtime, his first of the season. Lukas Dostal allowed six on 33 shots; Leevi Meriläinen gave up five on 23 and still got the win. Vancouver is 3-10-1. The Ducks are 5-6-1 and found the one way to lose to a team that had forgotten how to win: give up four goals in the last 12 minutes of hockey.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

BUF2SJS0Final: BUF 2, SJS 0

Yaroslav Askarov stopped 38 of 39 shots and lost, which is the San Jose experience in one sentence. Olen Zellweger scored 50 seconds into the second period, and that was the only puck anybody got past Askarov all night. Zach Benson's first of the season went into an empty net with 55 seconds left. At the other end Colten Ellis was barely needed and perfect when he was, stopping all 23 shots for the shutout. Owen Power assisted on both Buffalo goals. The Sabres improve to 5-4-3. The Sharks fall to 6-6-1 after getting outshot 39-23 at home, and a rebuild that leaves its best player stopping 38 shots alone is a rebuild that still has a long way to go.

Tuesday, October 27

Game recap

LAK6NYR3Final: LAK 6, NYR 3

The Rangers signed James Reimer on Sunday, started him Monday, and pulled him after one period. Welcome to Broadway, here's your hook. The Kings scored three times on Reimer's first eight shots: Taylor Ward 75 seconds in, Brandt Clarke with an extra attacker, and Drew Doughty late in the first. Dylan Garand came on and gave up two more in the second, Artemi Panarin on the power play back at the Garden and Mikey Anderson, and it was 5-1 before New York found a pulse. Doughty finished with a goal and two assists, Joel Edmundson added a goal and an assist with the empty-netter, and Darcy Kuemper made 23 saves on 26 shots. J.T. Miller, Adam Fox (his first goal after 16 points that were all assists) and Tye Kartye scored for the Rangers, who are 7-6-1 and have lost three straight. Los Angeles had won two games all season before this; New York made it look like a bye week.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

TOR2CGY5Final: TOR 2, CGY 5

The Leafs strolled into Calgary on a four-game win streak and left with a 5-2 loss and a fight story. Matvei Gridin scored twice, once on a power play 25 seconds into the second, and set up another, and Mikael Backlund came back from a two-game absence to score the second goal. It was 3-0 before Toronto showed up. Easton Cowan and William Nylander got it to 3-2 with 14 minutes left, but Joel Farabee and Martin Pospisil hit the empty net 46 seconds apart. Devin Cooley made 26 saves on 28 in his fourth straight start, Sergei Bobrovsky stopped 29 of 32, and Zack MacEwen and Jake Middleton fought in the first. Calgary has won four straight and is 5-6-0. Toronto drops to 7-5-2, proof that a hot streak in October lasts about as long as a Leafs playoff lead.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

DET4EDM3SOFinal: DET 4, EDM 3 SO

Michal Postava's first NHL start came in Edmonton against Connor McDavid, and he went 3-for-3 in the shootout against McDavid, Leon Draisaitl and Ryan Nugent-Hopkins. Some guys get a soft debut in Columbus. The Oilers led three times: Vasily Podkolzin in the first, Isaac Howard on the power play in the third and Colton Dach with 3:28 left. Detroit answered every time, through Viktor Arvidsson on the power play, Emmitt Finnie 30 seconds after Howard, and Dylan Larkin with the goalie pulled and 1:17 left, the man in every trade rumor making the play of the night. Lucas Raymond had two assists and scored the only shootout goal, Postava made 25 saves on 28, and Tristan Jarry stopped 26 of 29. Detroit is 5-4-3. Edmonton is 8-2-2 and found out that a lead with McDavid on the ice still isn't safe from its own defense.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Monday, October 26

Game recap

FLA3CHI2Final: FLA 3, CHI 2

Chicago scored 2:34 in, tied it in the second, and still found a way to lose, because that's the brand. Ryan Greene opened it from Mangiapane and Korchinski, Sandis Vilmanis answered, and Matthew Tkachuk put Florida ahead on the power play in the first. Roman Kantserov tied it at 2 in the second off a Kane-and-Bedard setup, the kind of play Chicago has been promising since the draft lottery. Then Lars Eller, of all people, scored the winner with 2:23 left, from Aaron Ekblad. Florida outshot Chicago 33-21; Akira Schmid made 19 saves and Spencer Knight 30. The Panthers are 6-4-2. The Blackhawks are 3-8-0 with three straight losses, and the only thing they're building faster than the rebuild is the losing streak.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

NYI3DAL6Final: NYI 3, DAL 6

The Islanders hung around for 40 minutes, answering every Dallas goal, then the third period showed up and the Stars ran them out of Texas. It was 3-3 after two, with Matthew Schaefer, Kyle Palmieri and Brayden Schenn scoring for New York, before Wyatt Johnston, Jason Robertson and Mikko Rantanen scored in the first 13:02 of the third. Robertson had two, Tyler Seguin a goal and an assist, and Justin Hryckowian got his first of the season on the power play. Dallas outshot New York 38-20; Jake Oettinger made 17 saves and Ilya Sorokin 32 on 38. The Stars have won five straight and sit at 7-3-1. The Islanders are 5-4-2, and they're learning that keeping it close for two periods counts for exactly as much as a moral victory in the standings.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

MTL2WPG1Final: MTL 2, WPG 1

Winnipeg threw 34 shots at Jacob Fowler and got one past him, which is the hockey version of buying 34 lottery tickets and winning a free coffee. Montreal's defensemen did the scoring: Lane Hutson at 7:19 of the second from Noah Dobson and Cole Caufield, then Kaiden Guhle 3:45 later, with Caufield setting him up again. Isak Rosen scored his first of the season with 4:36 left to make it interesting, and that was it. Fowler made 33 saves; Stuart Skinner stopped 19 of 21 at the other end. The Canadiens are 6-3-2 with two straight wins. The Jets are 4-4-3 and scoring 2.45 goals a game, and a team that just traded its franchise goalie can't afford a power outage this long.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

COL2NSH6Final: COL 2, NSH 6

Colorado spent Sunday night in the penalty box handing out power-play goals like party favors, and Nashville took four of them. The Predators were up 5-0 before the second intermission: Filip Forsberg on the power play, Steven Stamkos, Ryan O'Reilly on the power play, Jack Drury, and O'Reilly again with the extra man. Artturi Lehkonen (his 10th) and Devon Toews scored for Colorado, and Stamkos closed it on a fourth power-play goal. O'Reilly and Stamkos had two each and Roman Josi three assists. Parker Kelly and Jayden Struble fought in the second. Justus Annunen made 19 saves; Scott Wedgewood allowed six on 35. Nashville is 4-3-4. Colorado is 6-5-1 and 4-5-1 in its last 10, and a team built to win the Cup is killing penalties like it's never seen one before.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

MIN4VAN2Final: MIN 4, VAN 2

Quinn Hughes came back to Vancouver, heard the boos, and scored anyway, a power-play goal for his 500th career point, plus an assist for 501. Maxim Shabanov opened it on the power play, Bobby Brink scored his first of the season, and Kirill Kaprizov added his 13th early in the third to make it 4-0. Max Sasson and Brock Boeser scored late for Vancouver, which is a nice way of saying the Canucks woke up after the game was over. Calvin Pickard made 16 saves on 18 shots for his first win with the Wild; Leevi Meriläinen stopped 30 of 34. Minnesota is 8-3-2 and first in the Central. Vancouver is 2-10-1 and 10 straight games without a win, and the fans booing the guy who left might want to save some for the team that stayed.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →
