Sunday, October 25

Game recap

ANA5PHI4Final: ANA 5, PHI 4

Philadelphia built a 2-0 lead at home and then gave it away like free T-shirts. Matvei Michkov and Porter Martone scored on first-period power plays, Trevor Zegras set up both, and Tyson Foerster's shorthanded goal even had the Flyers ahead 3-2 in the second. Then Anaheim scored three straight: Judd Caulfield tied it late in the second, Tristan Luneau put the Ducks ahead two minutes into the third, and Beckett Sennecke made it 5-3 on the power play. Michkov's second of the night pulled Philly within one with almost 12 minutes left, and that was all. Luneau finished with a goal and two assists, Leo Carlsson a goal and an assist, and A.J. Greer scored, fought Hunter McDonald and piled up 17 penalty minutes. Lukas Dostal made 28 saves on 32 shots; Joseph Woll stopped 21 of 26. The Flyers are 3-7-3, and their plan for protecting a lead still looks like it was drawn on a napkin.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

LAK1NJD3Final: LAK 1, NJD 3

The Kings went to New Jersey and put 13 shots on goal in 60 minutes, which is less an offense than a rumor. Somehow they still led: Scott Laughton scored at 15:57 of the second. It lasted 2:46, until Anthony Mantha tied it before the intermission. Brett Pesce's first goal of the season put the Devils ahead midway through the third, and Arseny Gritsyuk hit the empty net with Jack Hughes and Jesper Bratt on the assists. Jake Allen had about as quiet a night as an NHL goalie gets, 12 saves on 13 shots, while Anton Forsberg stopped 23 of 25 to keep Los Angeles close. New Jersey is 7-4-0. The Kings are 2-5-2, and the shot clock in Newark barely needed batteries.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

SJS4BOS6Final: SJS 4, BOS 6

For 48 minutes San Jose looked like it might steal one in Boston. Then the Bruins scored three goals in 3:33. Casey Mittelstadt opened it, Michael Misa answered on the power play, Marat Khusnutdinov and Kiefer Sherwood (shorthanded) traded goals in the second, and Dmitry Orlov's power-play goal gave the Sharks a 3-2 lead early in the third. David Pastrnak tied it at 8:27, James Hagens scored 40 seconds later, and Fraser Minten made it 5-3 on the power play. Will Smith pulled San Jose within one, and Will Borgen sealed it into the empty net with 28 seconds left. JJ Peterka had two assists. Jeremy Swayman made 23 saves on 27 shots; Alex Nedeljkovic stopped 29 of 34. There were two fights, Michael Kesselring with Mark Kastelic and Tanner Jeannot with Zack Ostapchuk. Boston is 9-2-1. The Sharks are 6-5-1 and learned that a third-period lead in Boston has a shelf life of about four minutes.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

NYR4OTT7Final: NYR 4, OTT 7

Drake Batherson had a hat trick, and the Rangers' defense held the door for most of it. Ottawa led 2-0 seven minutes in on goals by Batherson and Tim Stützle, and 3-0 when Batherson scored again early in the second. New York made a game of it: Will Cuylle scored shorthanded, and after Dylan Cozens's first of the season, J.T. Miller and Alexis Lafrenière, with his ninth, made it 4-3 at the second intermission. Jake Sanderson, who finished with a goal and two assists, restored the two-goal lead, Pavel Dorofeyev pulled the Rangers within one with 4:28 left, and then the empty net did the rest: Michael Amadio, with Jonas Johansson credited with an assist, and Batherson with 12 seconds left for the hat trick. Johansson made 24 saves on 28 shots; Dylan Garand stopped 17 of 22. Ottawa is 8-4-0. The Rangers are 7-5-1, and Mike Sullivan spent the night shuffling his lines like a dealer who knows the deck is short.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

NSH2PIT3OTFinal: NSH 2, PIT 3 OT

Nashville was 66 seconds from a win in Pittsburgh and still left with just one point. Steven Stamkos opened the scoring in the first, Connor Dewar tied it 18 seconds into the second, and Jayden Struble's first of the season put the Predators back in front. Juuse Saros held that lead until 18:54 of the third, when the Penguins pulled Arturs Silovs and Rickard Rakell scored with Sidney Crosby and Erik Karlsson on the assists. Ville Koivunen ended it 3:44 into overtime. Saros made 34 saves on 37 shots and deserved better; Silovs stopped 24 of 26. Pittsburgh is 5-6-1. The Predators are 3-3-4, and four overtime and shootout losses in 10 games means they're collecting consolation points like participation medals.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

BUF3WSH4OTFinal: BUF 3, WSH 4 OT

Buffalo went up 2-0 in Washington on goals by Jack Quinn and Josh Doan in the first 11 minutes, and you can guess the rest. Alex Tuch got one back before the first intermission, and Dylan Strome scored twice in the second to put the Capitals ahead. Noah Ostlund tied it early in the third, with Rasmus Dahlin on the assist, and that held until Tuch beat Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen 3:42 into overtime, Strome and Jakob Chychrun assisting. Jordan Kyrou had two assists. Luukkonen made 30 saves on 34 shots; Charlie Lindgren stopped 18 of 21. Washington is 6-4-0. The Sabres are 4-4-3, and blowing a two-goal lead is about the most Buffalo way there is to collect a point.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

VGK1CBJ2OTFinal: VGK 1, CBJ 2 OT

The goalies ran this one. Denton Mateychuk put Columbus ahead in the first, Tomas Hertl tied it late in the period, and then nobody scored for more than 40 minutes because Cam Talbot and Carter Hart wouldn't allow it. A Vegas penalty in overtime gave the Blue Jackets a power play, and Adam Fantilli needed 59 seconds to end it, Charlie Coyle and Kent Johnson assisting. Talbot made 26 saves on 27 shots; Hart stopped 18 of 20. Columbus got there on 20 shots, which is efficient if not exactly thrilling, and is 4-5-0. Vegas is 8-4-1 and found out Columbus in October is no vacation.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

CAR4STL0Final: CAR 4, STL 0

Pyotr Kochetkov needed only 24 saves for a shutout in St. Louis, and Carolina did the rest at its leisure. Nobody scored in the first, and then the Hurricanes got three in the second: Sean Walker with an extra attacker on, Jesperi Kotkaniemi 20 seconds later, and Logan Stankoven's eighth. Nikolaj Ehlers added a power-play goal early in the third. Seth Jarvis and Sebastian Aho had two assists each. Carolina outshot the Blues 39-24, and Joel Hofer's 35 saves kept it from getting ugly. The Hurricanes are 9-2-2 with 20 points. The Blues are 5-5-1 and got shut out at home on 24 shots, a tough look for a team that sells itself on working hard.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

TOR7EDM2Final: TOR 7, EDM 2

Toronto went into Edmonton and hung seven on the Oilers, which is not a sentence anyone in Alberta enjoys reading. Jack Roslovic scored unassisted in the first, Auston Matthews and Troy Stecher scored 54 seconds apart in the second, and William Nylander added two in the third, one on the power play and one into the empty net. Zack MacEwen and Vinni Lettieri scored their first goals of the season, Lettieri's with 31 seconds left after he'd fought Connor Murphy in the second. Kirill Marchenko had two assists. Leon Draisaitl scored both Edmonton goals, each set up by Connor McDavid and Evan Bouchard, which is the Oilers' whole offense in one sentence. Anthony Stolarz made 30 saves on 32 shots; Tristan Jarry stopped 25 of 30. Toronto is 7-4-2. Edmonton is 8-2-1, and McDavid and Draisaitl with no help looks a lot like every Oilers June.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

TBL4UTA5OTFinal: TBL 4, UTA 5 OT

Tampa Bay led 3-1 in the first period and 4-2 in the second and still left Salt Lake with one point. Jake Guentzel, Pontus Holmberg and Brayden Point (on the power play, Nikita Kucherov assisting) built the early lead, and Conor Geekie made it 4-2 early in the second. Utah answered with Kailer Yamamoto, Dylan Guenther on the power play, Anders Lee and then defenseman Dmitri Simashev, who tied it late in the second and won it 1:44 into overtime. Vincent Trocheck had two assists, and Karel Vejmelka picked up one on the winner to go with 29 saves on 32 shots. Dennis Hildeby stopped 23 of 28, and Tampa played the third and overtime with 11 forwards after Zemgus Girgensons left the game. Utah is 8-4-0. The Lightning are 7-3-1 and found out a two-goal lead in the mountains thins out faster than the air.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

DET1CGY4Final: DET 1, CGY 4

Detroit's offense in Calgary was Andrew Copp and not much else. Joel Farabee put the Flames ahead late in the first and finished with a goal and two assists. Copp tied it early in the second, and then Calgary scored three more in the period: Zayne Parekh's first of the season on the power play, Ryan Strome, and Matvei Gridin, also on the power play, with 90 seconds left. Devin Cooley made 28 saves on 29 shots; John Gibson stopped 21 of 25. Ben Chiarot and Jake Middleton fought late in the third, by which point it was the only contest left. Calgary is 4-6-0. The Red Wings are 4-4-3, and giving up two power-play goals in one period is how a rebuild stays a rebuild.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

MIN5SEA1Final: MIN 5, SEA 1

Kirill Kaprizov scored 26 seconds in, his 12th of the season, and Seattle spent the rest of the night chasing. Berkly Catton tied it midway through the first, then Minnesota scored four straight: Blake Coleman, Olli Maatta, Joel Eriksson Ek and Coleman again into the empty net. Quinn Hughes assisted on the opener, and Jesper Wallstedt made 23 saves on 24 shots in the first half of a back-to-back. Joey Daccord stopped 31 of 35 as the Wild outshot the Kraken 36-24. Minnesota is 7-3-2. Seattle is 7-4-1 and spent the night proving a Kraken is a lot scarier in the movies.

Saturday, October 24

Game recap

MTL4CHI1Final: MTL 4, CHI 1

Connor Bedard scored 4:23 in, set up by Patrick Kane, and for about 13 minutes the United Center got to feel like the rebuild was over. Then Jake Evans happened. The Canadiens' checking center, not exactly the name on anyone's jersey, scored twice and added an assist, tying it late in the first and then going in shorthanded in the second, the kind of goal that should come with a refund for the Chicago power play. Kaiden Guhle made it 3-1 with 94 seconds left in the middle frame, Mike Matheson buried the empty-netter, and Montreal won 4-1 to move to 5-3-2. Jacob Fowler stopped 20 of 21 and spent most of the night watching. Spencer Knight made 24 saves on 27 shots, and Chicago managed 21 shots all game, which is about how many draft lottery balls it's been chasing since 2023. Now 3-7-0: Chicago keeps buying the rebuild, and the house keeps winning.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

TBL3COL6Final: TBL 3, COL 6

Tampa Bay walked into Ball Arena with one of the East's best records and was down 3-0 before the second period was half a minute old. Devon Toews scored 68 seconds in, Nazem Kadri added a power-play goal, and Fedor Svechkov scored 24 seconds into the second, which is roughly how long Andrei Vasilevskiy looked comfortable all night: 18 saves on 23 shots. Nathan MacKinnon had a goal and three assists because of course he did, Martin Necas had a goal and two helpers including the empty-netter, and Artturi Lehkonen picked up his ninth. Jake Guentzel scored twice, once on the power play, and Charle-Edouard D'Astous got it to 5-3 late, but Mackenzie Blackwood made 31 saves on 34 shots and the Lightning never got closer than two in the last 50 minutes. Colorado wins 6-3 and moves to 6-4-1. Tampa drops to 7-3-0 and flies to Utah tonight, where at least the altitude is lower.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Ville Koivunen scored 3:44 into overtime and Silovs made 24 saves. Malkin missed the game with an illness. The Penguins (5-6-1) have won two straight.

Dylan Strome scored twice and set up the winner, and Sourdif returned from his illness with an assist. Buffalo led 2-0 after the first.

Puckline's Report

Logan Cooley scored a hat trick and added an assist, Utah led three separate times, and the Mammoth still flew out of Montreal with one point. Cooley went 9, 10, 11 on the season, two of them on the power play, and Nick Schmaltz's power-play goal made it 4-3 early in the third. Every time, the Canadiens came back: Nick Suzuki (a goal, two assists), Arber Xhekaj, who scored his first and then dropped the gloves with Liam O'Brien four seconds later, Kirby Dach, and Adam Engstrom, whose first of the year tied it 4-4 with five minutes left. Cole Caufield needed 30 seconds of overtime for his 11th, set up by Lane Hutson and Suzuki. Jakub Dobes stopped only 16 of 20, Sebastian Cossa 30 of 35. Montreal is 10-3-3. Utah held the lead for most of the night and handed it back three times: that's not a lead, that's a timeshare.

Puckline's Report

Forty minutes of nothing, then a third period worth the price of admission, and Vegas took it 2-1 in Detroit. Anton Johansson finally broke the ice for the Red Wings two minutes into the third, and the lead lasted all of 2:18 before Braeden Bowman tied it. Then, with 1:42 left, Trevor Connelly buried his seventh from Jack Eichel and Rasmus Andersson, and the Little Caesars Arena crowd went home with cold pizza. Carter Hart was the reason it got that far, stopping 25 of 26, while Daniil Tarasov made 32 saves on 34 shots in a game the Wings had no business staying in. Vegas is 11-5-2. Detroit falls to 7-7-3, one goal on a night it needed two. Hockeytown has been rebuilding so long the blueprints are on microfiche.

Puckline's Report

Tampa Bay is now 8-0 at home, and Chicago never looked like the team to change that. Victor Hedman opened it on the power play four minutes in, Ilya Mikheyev scored late in the first, and early in the third Ryan McDonagh and Mikheyev again made it 4-0 inside three minutes. Zemgus Girgensons came back from his lower-body injury ahead of schedule and set up Mikheyev's second. Andrei Vasilevskiy stopped 25 of 26, and the one he missed was Roman Kantserov's with 50 seconds left, which is the closest thing to a highlight the Blackhawks had. Dillon Boucher and Jeffrey Viel fought early in the second. Arvid Soderblom made 31 saves on 35 shots. The Lightning are 10-3-2. Chicago is 4-12-1, and in a rebuild like this, spoiling the shutout counts as a win.

Puckline's Report

New Jersey led 4-1 after two periods and still needed Jesper Bratt in overtime. The Devils built it with a goal from Luke Hughes, two from Anthony Mantha and one from Jesper Boqvist, with Mantha's second coming 19 seconds after Boqvist's; Jack Hughes had two assists. Then St. Louis woke up. Mason McTavish scored midway through the third, Philip Broberg made it 4-3, and Dalibor Dvorsky tied it 18 seconds later with 5:06 to go. Bratt settled it 1:26 into overtime, from Dougie Hamilton. Connor Hellebuyck stopped 28 of 32, and Jordan Binnington made 31 saves on 36 shots. Jake Neighbours and Timo Meier fought early in the second. The Devils are 11-5-0. The Blues scored three goals in 3:08 to rescue a game they'd spent two periods losing, then got a loser point for it, which is the most St. Louis outcome possible.

Puckline's Report

Carolina scored twice in the first 3:20, the Islanders tied it twice, and the league's best team won it anyway, 5-3 at UBS Arena. Logan Stankoven scored 57 seconds in and Jesperi Kotkaniemi added another. Mitchell Chaffee (his first) and Brayden Schenn tied it early in the second; Andrei Svechnikov put Carolina back in front a minute later, and Victor Eklund tied it again before the second intermission. The winner came from the least likely name on the sheet: William Carrier, his first of the season with 5:08 left, from Svechnikov and Sebastian Aho. Jalen Chatfield added the empty-netter. Brandon Bussi stopped 24 of 27, Semyon Varlamov 34 of 38. The Hurricanes are 13-3-2. The Islanders, still without Mathew Barzal and Ryan Pulock, are 7-6-2, and they made their fans watch a fourth-liner decide it.

Puckline's Report

Philadelphia had a third-period lead at Madison Square Garden and gave it back in 89 seconds. Gabe Perreault scored first for the Rangers, then Simon Benoit (his first of the year) and Noel Acciari scored two minutes apart in the second to put the Flyers up 2-1. It held until 13:52 of the third, when Pavel Dorofeyev tied it on the power play, and Tye Kartye won it at 15:21, with Adam Fox assisting on both. Dylan Garand stopped 23 of 25 for New York, and Joseph Woll made 25 saves on 28 shots for Philadelphia. The Rangers are 9-7-1. The Flyers fall to 4-10-4. For an offense that scores less than anyone, two goals is a hot streak, and they still couldn't hold it through the third.

Puckline's Report

Justin Brazeau gave Pittsburgh a 1-0 lead nine minutes in, and Boston answered with six of the next seven goals. Pavel Zacha, Mark Kastelic and Elias Lindholm, unassisted, scored in the last eight minutes of the first. Nick Robertson got the Penguins back within 3-2 early in the second, then Zacha scored again, Morgan Geekie made it 5-2 and Fraser Minten added the sixth in the third. David Pastrnak and JJ Peterka each had two assists, both on Zacha's goals. Michael DiPietro only had to stop 16 of 18. At the other end, Arturs Silovs saw 24 shots and stopped 18, which is how you get to 5-9-2. The Bruins are 12-4-1. Pittsburgh's lead lasted three minutes and its defense never showed up, which is about how this season has gone for a franchise that keeps insisting it isn't rebuilding.

Puckline's Report

Two goalies, 65 minutes and one goal each, and Columbus won the skills competition. Cam Talbot and Casey DeSmith made it scoreless through two periods, and Mikko Rantanen's ninth, from Wyatt Johnston, looked like enough for Dallas midway through the third. Then Zach Werenski scored his first goal of the season with 3:14 left, from Kent Johnson and Matthew Knies, and the Blue Jackets never trailed again. In the shootout Valeri Nichushkin and Kent Johnson scored; Jason Robertson and Tyler Seguin didn't. Talbot finished with 27 saves on 28 shots plus both shootout attempts, and DeSmith stopped 29 of 30. Columbus is 7-7-0 with two straight wins. Dallas, without Miro Heiskanen, is 9-5-2. The Stars put one puck past Talbot in 65 minutes and none in the shootout, and that offense couldn't pass a referendum either.

Puckline's Report

Winnipeg went nine games without a win; now it has two in a row, and Vancouver was happy to help. Alex Iafallo scored on the power play at 3:49 and Cole Koepke added another 14 seconds later. Liam Ohgren answered for the Canucks, but Dawson Mercer scored his first of the season before the first intermission, Neal Pionk and Mark Scheifele scored in the second, and Mario Ferraro made it 6-1 in the third. Kyle Connor and Dylan DeMelo each had two assists, and Scheifele had a goal and an assist. Brock Boeser scored late. Stuart Skinner stopped 24 of 26 for the Jets, and Leevi Meriläinen gave up six on 29 shots. Winnipeg is 6-8-3. Vancouver is 3-14-1, the league's worst, and has become the team you play when you need to feel good about yourself again.

Puckline's Report

Pavel Mintyukov had the full Gordie Howe hat trick, and Anaheim held on in Edmonton, 5-4. Cutter Gauthier opened it on the power play, Evan Bouchard answered on one, and Connor McDavid scored shorthanded early in the second to make it 2-1 Oilers. Then the Ducks scored four straight: Mintyukov twice, his first two of the season, three minutes apart, and Beckett Sennecke twice, the second on the power play early in the third. Mintyukov also set up Sennecke's first and fought Kasperi Kapanen in the first period. Edmonton came back late: Kapanen on the power play, then Leon Draisaitl at 19:15 with the goalie pulled, but time ran out. McDavid had a goal and two assists. Laurent Brossoit stopped 23 of 27; Matt Tomkins 16 of 21. Edmonton is 11-3-3. Five goals on 21 shots: the Oilers' goaltending search goes on, now in its second decade.

Puckline's Report

Nashville goes past regulation again, and this time Steven Stamkos made it count. Ross Colton opened the scoring, Jaden Schwartz tied it, Vitali Pinchuk put the Predators back in front with his first of the season, and Parker Kelly tied it early in the second. After that, nothing for 37 minutes, until Stamkos scored on the power play 2:18 into overtime, from Roman Josi and Ryan O'Reilly. Justus Annunen was the story in the Nashville net, stopping 30 of 32 at Ball Arena, while Mackenzie Blackwood made 22 saves on 25 shots. Colorado tried a new top pair, with Sam Malinski beside Devon Toews and Cale Makar moved to Brett Kulak's side, and got two goals out of 32 shots for the trouble. The Predators are 7-4-5. The Avalanche, 9-6-2, have one of the league's best attacks and got outscored by Vitali Pinchuk and Ross Colton.

CBJ @ BUF · 7:00 PM ET

Columbus Blue JacketsCBJ7-7-0 · 14 PTSML +146
@7:00 PM ETFri Nov 6 · KeyBank Center
CBJ +146MLBUF -176
Buffalo SabresBUF7-5-3 · 17 PTSML -176

Puckline Preview

Columbus rolls into Buffalo on the second night of a back-to-back, fresh off beating Dallas in a shootout, and these two last met on opening night, when the Blue Jackets won 6-3 in Columbus. The Jackets are 7-7-0 with two straight wins and have played the fewest games in the league. Zach Werenski finally scored his first goal of the season last night with 3:14 left, which for a defenseman with 12 assists counts as breaking a long fast. Kent Johnson leads them with 14 points and is 2-for-2 in shootouts, and Columbus is 2-0 when it gets that far. Cam Talbot played last night, so Jet Greaves gets the start, with Elvis Merzlikins still out after shoulder surgery. Steven Lorentz and Jack Williams are up from Cleveland, Lorentz after seven goals in nine AHL games, but neither is expected to dress.

Buffalo is 7-5-3 and lost 2-1 to Ottawa on Wednesday after sweeping California. Tage Thompson has 10 goals and 18 points, and Lindy Ruff is rotating goalies through a busy stretch, so this time Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen is expected in net. Jiri Kulich is back from a concussion and Conor Timmins makes his season debut on the blue line. The Sabres have spent a decade promising that this is the year. In November, it usually still looks like it.

By Puckline Prince

SJS @ MIN · 8:00 PM ET

San Jose SharksSJS7-9-1 · 15 PTSML +220
@8:00 PM ETFri Nov 6 · Grand Casino Arena
SJS +220MLMIN -275
Minnesota WildMIN11-3-3 · 25 PTSML -275

Puckline Preview

First meeting of the season, and the gap in the standings is wide: Minnesota is 11-3-3, first in the Central, with two straight wins, while San Jose is 7-9-1 and has lost three in a row by a combined 14-4. Kirill Kaprizov leads the league with 15 goals, Quinn Hughes has 22 points from the back end, and Jesper Wallstedt, in net again tonight, has started 15 of 17 games, going 10-2-3 with a .919. The Wild are doing it without Brock Faber and Jared Spurgeon, who are both out again tonight, with Filip Gustavsson out and both Folignos game-time decisions. Somehow the team keeps winning with half its blue line in street clothes.

The Sharks have Macklin Celebrini, 17 points, and not much else that's working. Yaroslav Askarov is 4-7-0 with an .887 and gave up seven in Los Angeles on Wednesday. Eric Pohlkamp, a defenseman called up this week, made his NHL debut in that game, which is a rough way to meet the league. Pierre LeBrun says Mike Grier isn't thinking about a coaching change, and Ryan Warsofsky would probably like the Sharks to stop giving people reasons to ask.

By Puckline Prince

ANA @ CGY · 8:00 PM ET

Anaheim DucksANA8-7-1 · 17 PTSML +125
@8:00 PM ETFri Nov 6 · Scotiabank Saddledome
ANA +125MLCGY -150
Calgary FlamesCGY7-8-1 · 15 PTSML -150

Puckline Preview

Anaheim has scored five or more goals in six straight games, a franchise first, and it finishes its road trip in Calgary on the second night of a back-to-back after a 5-4 win in Edmonton. Cutter Gauthier has nine goals in his last four games, Beckett Sennecke has 10 on the season, Leo Carlsson leads the team with 24 points, and Pavel Mintyukov had two goals, an assist and a fight against the Oilers. The defense is another story: the Ducks have given up four or more in four of their last five. Laurent Brossoit has started three straight, so Lukas Dostal is the probable starter, and Troy Terry is out for the rest of the trip.

Calgary is 7-8-1 and scores 2.44 goals a game, about as far from Anaheim's 3.69 as you can get. Joel Farabee leads with 16 points, Dustin Wolf has an .870 and Jonathan Huberdeau is out. These two have split the season series: Anaheim won 4-2 in Calgary on October 10, and the Flames won 4-2 in Anaheim three nights later. If the Ducks keep it up, Calgary's offense will need its best night of the season, which so far is not saying much.

By Puckline Prince
